abstract: OBJECTIVE: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is a critical-priority pathogen. We investigated the epidemiological characteristics and clinical outcomes of Acinetobacter baumannii infections over an 11-year period at a tertiary hospital in northern China. METHODS: We analysed 4,028 A. baumannii isolates from a single tertiary hospital (2014-2024; first isolate per patient-year), calculating resistance rates, annual CRAB proportion, antibiotic consumption (DDDs/100 patient-days, 2018-2024) and in-hospital mortality; testing used the Cochran-Armitage test and Spearman correlation. RESULTS: The CRAB proportion fell from 62.2% (2014) to 37.8% (2024; p<0.001) while antibiotic consumption rose by 29.2%. Resistance was near-universal, sparing only minocycline (4.6%) and polymyxin (0.3%). No agent's resistance rate was significantly correlated with its consumption (|ρ| ≤ 0.71; all p ≥ 0.09). In 1,811 patient-episodes (35.2% mortality), older age (OR 1.20 per 10 years), intensive-care admission (1.86), mechanical ventilation (1.74) and male sex (1.25) each independently predicted death; empirical therapy covered only 2.6% of isolates. CONCLUSIONS: CRAB was predominantly detected in intensive care units and was closely associated with mechanical ventilation, representing a major nosocomial pathogen. Given its high associated mortality, continuous surveillance of its epidemiological characteristics is warranted.

abstract: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) involving the central nervous system (CNS) represent a critical challenge, with mortality of 50% or more in cerebral aspergillosis, mucormycosis, fusariosis and cryptococcal meningitis, and pharmacokinetic (PK) access restricted by the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This review analyzes the clinical performance and parenchymal penetration of isavuconazole (ISA), a second-generation triazole. ISA exhibits linear PK, a cyclodextrin-free intravenous formulation, and high tissue affinity, favored by moderate lipophilicity (experimental logP 2.56) and in vitro inhibition of P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) efflux transporters. Experimental evidence from animal models shows brain-to-plasma ratios of 0.42 to 1.8, indicating efficient BBB crossing. Human biopsy data show a fundamental PK dichotomy. While cerebrospinal fluid concentrations are restricted (about 1% of plasma), levels in fungal abscesses and inflamed parenchyma reach up to 5.11 mg/L, exceeding the minimum inhibitory concentration reported for Aspergillus fumigatus in those cases. Clinically, ISA was associated with a response in 70% of first-line (n = 10) and 73% of salvage-treated patients (n = 30) with cerebral aspergillosis, and 82% of 28 patients with CNS-only coccidioidomycosis improved or stabilized. Meta-analyses suggest fewer drug-related adverse events and, in randomized subgroups, fewer hepatobiliary events compared with voriconazole, although moderate cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibition warrants monitoring of calcineurin and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors in transplant recipients. ISA is a strategic option for high-complexity CNS-involving IFIs, serving as a therapeutic alternative in salvage and prolonged-maintenance settings, though first-line use in CNS infection awaits confirmation from randomized trials. Central nervous system fungal infections are hard to treat because few drugs reach the affected tissue. This review shows that isavuconazole, a second-generation extended-spectrum azole, penetrates brain tissue and is linked to clinical responses, although the evidence is mostly retrospective.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Lung transplant recipients (LTRs) with cystic fibrosis (CF) are frequently colonized with multidrug-resistant pathogens, including extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), which increase peri-transplant morbidity. Bacteriophage therapy (BT) has shown efficacy against XDR bacteria, but its prophylactic use post-transplant has rarely been reported. CASE PRESENTATION: A 46-year-old woman with CF and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome stage III) after bilateral lung transplantation in 2005 underwent retransplantation in 2024. She was colonized with XDR PA and Aspergillus spp. Peri-transplant prophylaxis included ceftolozane/tazobactam, intravenous and inhaled colistin, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, and intravenous liposomal amphotericin B. BT was personalized based on phage susceptibility testing (PST) and initiated immediately post-transplant via combined intravenous and endobronchial administration for three weeks. Pulmonary cultures remained negative for XDR PA during this period. The patient ultimately developed multiorgan failure unrelated to XDR PA and died 88 days post-transplant. CONCLUSION: This is one of the first reported case of prophylactic BT in lung transplantation, achieving pulmonary microbiologic suppression of XDR PA. While the patient's outcome was determined by other complications. Prospective studies are needed to define its efficacy, safety, and optimal administration.

abstract: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) is an underrecognized but significant sequela of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), and data from India remain limited. In this single-center, cross-sectional study from eastern India, we evaluated 280 post-TB patients with residual radiological abnormalities to estimate CPA prevalence and identify associated clinical, radiological, and biochemical features. After excluding patients with active TB, interstitial lung disease, malignancy, or prior antifungal therapy, all participants underwent clinical assessment, spirometry, high-resolution computed tomography, Aspergillus-specific serology, and bronchoalveolar lavage when indicated. CPA was diagnosed in 27.5% of patients, with chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis being the most common subtype. Multivariable analysis showed that low body mass index, the presence of aspergilloma, and elevated C-reactive protein were independently associated with CPA, while Aspergillus-specific IgG was positive in 92.2% of cases. These findings highlight the high burden of CPA among post-TB patients in India and underscore the need for greater clinician awareness and standardized screening to ensure timely diagnosis and management.

abstract: Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia (TPE) and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) share cough, wheeze, eosinophilia, and marked immunoglobulin (Ig) E elevation and may coexist in patients with asthma in filariasis-endemic settings. We prospectively characterized this overlap phenotype at a tertiary respiratory center in eastern India. Eligible patients older than 10 years had a documented prior physician diagnosis of asthma and, at presentation, an absolute eosinophil count (AEC) >1000 cells/µL and total IgE >1000 IU/mL; all underwent evaluation for both TPE and ABPA. These laboratory thresholds were study-entry criteria and were not substituted for disease-specific diagnostic definitions. TPE attribution required a compatible clinic-serological profile and a study-defined post-diethylcarbamazine (DEC) haematological response of at least 50% reduction in AEC. For the present analysis, ABPA was classified according to the revised 2024 International Society for Human and Animal Mycology criteria using prospectively collected clinical, immunological, and imaging variables. In TPE-compatible patients, DEC was given before ABPA-directed therapy to preserve interpretation of the eosinophilic response. Among 312 prospectively evaluated patients, 132 met the study definitions for TPE-ABPA overlap, 77 for TPE alone, and 103 for ABPA alone.  In the overlap cohort, mean age was 36.2±15.9 years; median baseline AEC was 6071 cells/µL [interquartile range (IQR) 3793-11,000] and median total IgE was 7641 IU/mL (IQR 4525-13,621). Aspergillus fumigatus-specific IgE and IgG were positive in all 132; the filarial antigen was positive in 128 (97.0%), and there was qualitative filarial IgG in all 132.  The dominant recorded high-resolution computed tomography pattern was normal in 73 (55.3%), while bronchiectasis was recorded in 42 (31.8%). All overlap patients received DEC and fulfilled the study-defined ≥50% AEC response criterion. ABPA-directed treatment comprised systemic corticosteroids alone in 71 (53.8%), itraconazole alone in 41 (31.1%), and both in 20 (15.2%). Concurrent TPE and ABPA should be considered in endemic regions when asthma is accompanied by disproportionate eosinophilia and IgE elevation; recognition of one eosinophilic disorder should not prematurely terminate evaluation for the other.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Necrotising soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rapidly progressive infections requiring prompt diagnosis and management. This study assessed predictors of mortality, microbiological spectrum, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and differences between polymicrobial and monomicrobial NSTIs in a prospective manner. METHODS: This study enrolled patients aged 15 years or older with clinically suspected NSTIs who presented between March 2022 and February 2023. Clinical, laboratory, surgical, and outcome data were collected. Tissue and pus samples were processed for aerobic and anaerobic cultures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed according to CLSI guidelines. Mortality-associated factors were analysed using univariate analysis, binary logistic regression, and survival analysis. RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients were included, predominantly male (87.3%), with a median age of 47.5 years. Extremities were most commonly affected. The mortality rate of this cohort was 25.3%. Polymicrobial infections predominated (49.4%), while monomicrobial NSTIs were associated with higher mortality (p = 0.022). Gram-negative organisms, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, were the most frequent pathogens. Obligate anaerobes were significantly associated with polymicrobial infections. Chronic liver disease (p = 0.003) and systemic toxicity (p = 0.018) independently predicted mortality, whereas higher haemoglobin levels were protective. High antimicrobial resistance was observed, including carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii and Enterobacterales. Among the anaerobes, resistance to clindamycin and cefoxitin, along with reduced susceptibility to metronidazole, was reported. CONCLUSION: NSTIs remain associated with substantial mortality, especially in monomicrobial infections due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens. Early recognition, prompt surgery, and region-specific empirical antimicrobial therapy are crucial for improving outcomes.

Eligibility: People aged 12 to 65 years with APECED and severe AA. Design: Participants will be in this study for up to 10 months. abstract: Pulmonary mucormycosis is an aggressive, angioinvasive fungal infection that carries high mortality. Endobronchial involvement is rare and may present as a pedunculated mass with associated parenchymal consolidation, mimicking lung cancer. We present a case of a 52-year-old male smoker with poorly controlled Type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a history of pulmonary tuberculosis 19 years prior presented with a 6-month history of cough and hemoptysis. Suspecting tuberculosis reactivation, he was empirically treated with anti-tuberculosis therapy (ATT) for 6 months without clinical response. High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the chest revealed a 4.9 cm hyperdense necrotic consolidation patch with internal calcification in the right upper lobe (RUL). Flexible video-bronchoscopy demonstrated a pedunculated mass in the posterior segment of the RUL, clinically concerning for lung cancer. Biopsy of tissue revealed extensive necrosis, hyalinization and thick-walled, broad, non-septate fungal hyphae with characteristic right-angle branching and spores, confirming pulmonary mucormycosis without evidence of malignancy or granulomatous disease. Endobronchial mucormycosis should be considered in patients with diabetes, chronic airway disease or post-tuberculosis lung disease who present with non-resolving endobronchial masses. Early bronchoscopic tissue sampling is essential to avoid delayed diagnosis and inappropriate empirical therapy.

abstract: There is an intricate link between bronchiectasis and fungi. Patients with cystic fibrosis frequently manifest fungal sensitization and fungal colonization with Aspergillus fumigatus.6 Aspergillus species also has a cause-and-effect relationship with non-CF (cystic fibrosis) bronchiectasis.7, 8 In allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), Aspergillus is the cause of bronchiectasis. In contrast, in other causes of bronchiectasis, A fumigatus can theoretically promote allergic response, which may result in poor lung function, increase the risk of exacerbations, and even cause ABPA over time.9, 10 In a recent study, we found an overall prevalence of Aspergillus sensitization of 29.5% and the prevalence of chronic aspergillus infection was 76%.11 The prevalence of chronic aspergillus colonization in non-(tuberculosis) TB-non-CF fibrosis was 47.5% (49/103).11 By mechanism similar to chronic bacterial colonization, chronic aspergillus infection or aspergillus sensitization can increase the risk of bronchiectasis exacerbation. Therefore, eradication of A. fumigatus from the airways of patients with bronchiectasis would decrease the future risk of a bronchiectasis exacerbation. Notably, in ABPA, use of itraconazole and voriconazole reduce the exacerbations by reducing the fungal burden in the airways.12, 13 In this randomized trial, we will investigate whether treatment with oral itraconazole for six months would reduce the future risk of bronchiectasis exacerbation in patients with non-CF-non-ABPA bronchiectasis.

abstract: Patients with leukemia are treated with intensive chemotherapy and often have to undergo a stem cell transplantation which makes their immune system extremely vulnerable. This puts them at risk for invasive fungal infections, of which invasive mucormycosis (IM) is one of the most dangerous ones. Treatment of IM is complex and mortality rates are still extremely high, ranging from 40% to 80% and sometimes even higher if the central nervous system is involved. Mucormycosis requires immediate intervention due to the rapidly progressive and destructive nature of the infection. But the diagnosis is often made too late… Better survival can be achieved with a faster diagnosis. A new test has recently been developed for detection of Mucorales DNA by PCR. The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a method that allows to quickly make millions of copies of, for example, Mucorales DNA in order to detect it in the blood at an early stage. Because blood can easily be obtained, without an additional burden on the patient, the test could be interesting for screening for these infections, which then offers the opportunity to start an adequate treatment more quickly. However, the test is now only performed if there is a clinical suspicion of IM. But at that point, precious time has already been lost, and often the patient can no longer be cured. In this study the utility of the Mucorales PCR as a possible screening test in at-risk patients is assessed. The participants, hospitalised patients with leukemia, will be screened twice weekly with a Mucorales PCR test during their most vulnerable period. If the study shows that the test helps in diagnosing IM faster, this could have an important impact on the treatment and survival of these at-risk patients.

abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. METHOD: A retrospective case series study was conducted. Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. RESULTS: A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. CONCLUSION: In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

abstract: BACKGROUND: When tuberculosis is complicated by fungal infection, voriconazole and antituberculosis drugs may need to be used in combination, and drug interactions can affect efficacy and safety. METHODS: This structured narrative review used a systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) from database inception to May 2026, together with predefined eligibility criteria and evidence stratification. Clinical pharmacokinetic, therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), observational, case-report, and case-series studies were eligible as the primary evidence base. Relevant RESULTS: A total of 2,198 records were identified, and 17 primary clinical studies were included. Most were case reports or small retrospective studies, with limited paired antituberculosis-drug exposure data and clinical outcomes; generalizability is therefore limited. Existing clinical pharmacokinetic evidence is concentrated on rifamycins. Rifampicin markedly reduces voriconazole exposure and its induction may persist after discontinuation, so coadministration should be avoided. Rifapentine can also substantially lower voriconazole concentrations, with interindividual variability in the offset of induction; dose adjustment and re-initiation after withdrawal require serial TDM. Rifabutin has a bidirectional interaction: it can reduce voriconazole exposure, while voriconazole may increase exposure to rifabutin and its active metabolite. Current U.S. voriconazole labeling lists rifabutin coadministration as contraindicated, and rare off-label case experience does not establish it as a safe alternative. For isoniazid, ethambutol, linezolid, and other non-rifamycin agents, available evidence is mechanistic or hypothesis-generating and does not establish causal interactions or justify empirical voriconazole dose adjustment. CONCLUSION: Management should prioritize avoidance of voriconazole coadministration with rifampicin and rifabutin in accordance with current labeling, and avoidance of rifapentine where feasible. If rifapentine exposure cannot be avoided or has recently stopped, serial TDM should guide voriconazole dosing. For non-rifamycin antituberculosis drugs, monitoring should be matched to the suspected risk (exposure variability, QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity, or optic, neurologic, or hematologic toxicity) rather than based on unvalidated empirical dose changes.

abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study established a population pharmacokinetic model of voriconazole with the aim of adjusting the dosing regimen of voriconazole. METHODS: This was a retrospective study in which clinical data from 3,002 patients were collected from their medical records. Based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, this study included data from 96 patients to establish a population pharmacokinetic model. Following model evaluation, a dosing adjustment regimen for voriconazole was derived using Monte Carlo simulation and validated in a clinical setting. RESULTS: The study used a one-compartment model to fit the data, with a exponential model selected for inter-individual variability and a mixed model selected for residual variability. The model results showed that the CL of voriconazole was 4.2 L/h and the V was 75.9 L. CL was significantly correlated with creatinine clearance (CCr), and C-reactive protein (CRP), while V was significantly correlated with whether omeprazole was used in combination. According to Monte Carlo simulation results: If the trough concentration is <0.5 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be increased by 95%. If the trough concentration is ≥ 0.5 mg/L and <1.0 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be increased by 65%. If the trough concentration is > 5.5 and ≤7.5 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be decreased by 35%. If the trough concentration is > 7.5 and ≤10.0 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be decreased by 55%. If the trough concentration is > 10.0 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be decreased by 75%. In the clinical validation study, a total of 67 patients met the new inclusion and exclusion criteria and were included in the validation analysis. Of these 67 patients, after up to three dose adjustments based on the recommendations of the population pharmacokinetic model, 61 patients (91.04%) achieved steady-state plasma concentrations within the target range. CONCLUSION: 67 patients participated in the clinical validation study. The results showed that among the 67 patients who followed the standard treatment regimen described in the package insert, 46.3% achieved the target concentration range. After applying the dose adjustment regimen derived from this study, the proportion of patients achieving the target concentration range increased to 91.04%.

abstract: Drug dosing during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is difficult in critically ill patients because drug exposure is influenced by both the patient and the extracorporeal treatment. This narrative review provides a practical overview of drug dosing during CRRT, while intermittent hemodialysis and sustained low-efficiency dialysis are discussed only where they provide relevant contextual or comparative information. It summarizes the main drug-related, patient-related, and treatment-related factors that influence extracorporeal drug clearance and discusses their clinical implications for commonly used drug classes. Loading and maintenance doses should be considered separately: loading doses depend mainly on volume of distribution and the need for early therapeutic exposure, whereas maintenance dosing depends on total clearance, including residual renal, extracorporeal, and non-renal clearance. Therapeutic drug monitoring can help guide dose adjustment when validated targets are available, while model-informed precision dosing may provide additional support in selected patients. The review also proposes an eight-step practical framework based on residual kidney function, the actual delivered CRRT prescription, drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, therapeutic monitoring, and repeated reassessment. Future approaches may combine real-time CRRT data with pharmacokinetic models to support more individualized dosing.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal pneumonia remains a diagnostic challenge in immunocompromised children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), as conventional microbiological tests have limited sensitivity. This retrospective study evaluated whether serial chest computed tomography (CT) scored with the Radiologic Severity Index (RSI) was associated with initiation of antifungal therapy in 87 children with ALL and chemotherapy-related pneumonia. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 87 pediatric patients [median age 6.2 years, interquartile range (IQR) 3.5-8.0 years] diagnosed with ALL who developed pneumonia during chemotherapy between March 2016 and October 2024. Demographic data, medical history, and laboratory findings were collected for each patient. Chest CT images were assessed using the RSI, which quantifies affected lung volume and regional opacity (range 0-48). Clinical and radiologic characteristics of fungal and non-fungal pneumonia cases were compared using t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Pearson's Chi-squared tests, or Fisher's exact tests. Additionally, binary logistic regression models were employed to examine the correlation between RSI and antifungal therapy initiation. RESULTS: No significant differences in baseline or peak RSI were observed between fungal and non-fungal groups, nor between antifungal-treated and untreated groups (all P>0.05). Routine laboratory parameters, including leukocyte, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts, as well as serum albumin levels, did not differ between groups (all P>0.05). However, the antifungal-treated group demonstrated significantly higher change from baseline to peak Radiologic Severity Index (ΔRSI) (P=0.01) and RSI variation rate (P=0.02) compared to the untreated group. In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for potential confounders, neither ΔRSI [odds ratio (OR) =1.14, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.94-1.37, P=0.18] nor RSI variation rate (OR =0.54, 95% CI: 0.15-1.98, P=0.36) emerged as an independent predictor of antifungal therapy initiation. CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic RSI metrics (ΔRSI and RSI variation rate) are significantly elevated in pediatric ALL patients with chemotherapy-related pneumonia who receive antifungal therapy, whereas static RSI metrics and routine laboratory parameters are not. However, after adjusting for clinical confounders, dynamic RSI metrics do not independently predict antifungal treatment initiation. These findings suggest that serial CT monitoring and dynamic RSI assessment may reflect clinically meaningful disease progression, but current evidence does not support their use as standalone predictive tools for antifungal therapy decisions. Prospective studies with standardized imaging protocols are warranted to validate these exploratory results.

abstract: Nasopharyngeal mucormycosis is exceptionally rare, with only three prior cases reported. We describe a 19-year-old male without prior medical illness who presented with progressive left ear pain that was initially managed as external otitis. Three weeks later, he developed diabetic ketoacidosis from newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus. During hospitalization, bilateral complete facial nerve paralysis (House-Brackmann grade 6) developed on consecutive days. Computed tomography showed only nasopharyngeal mucosal thickening, but direct nasopharyngoscopy revealed a necrotic mass. Histopathology confirmed acute invasive mucormycosis. The patient received liposomal amphotericin B for one month, underwent endoscopic debridement, and was discharged on oral posaconazole for two months. The fungal infection resolved completely, but the bilateral facial palsy showed no improvement. This case represents the fourth reported instance of nasopharyngeal mucormycosis and the first in a previously healthy young adult presenting with bilateral complete facial nerve palsy. The clinical course emphasizes that new-onset diabetic ketoacidosis alone can create sufficient susceptibility for invasive mucormycosis even in immunocompetent individuals. Furthermore, severe cranial neuropathy may precede any typical radiographic findings, making prompt endoscopic evaluation and empirical antifungal therapy critical. Despite successful infection eradication, neurological deficits can persist as permanent sequelae.

abstract: Microcystin-LR (MC-LR) is a widely distributed cyanotoxin in freshwater ecosystems. Given the slow degradation of MC-LR in sediments and the overlapping benthic habitat of the Chinese mitten crab Eriocheir sinensis, this study investigated the effects of 28-day exposure to gradient concentrations of MC-LR (1, 10 and 20 μg·L⁻¹) on gill tissue. The results demonstrated that MC-LR exposure reduced the hepatosomatic index (HSI), weight gain rate, and survival rate, while inducing gill tissue lesions, with more pronounced effects observed in the medium and high concentration groups. Oxidative stress indicators, including the gene expression levels of cat, gclc, gpx, and nrf2, as well as the contents of ROS, MDA, H₂O₂, and T-AOC, were elevated across all three treatment groups, reaching maximum levels in TG3. Expression levels of osmoregulation-related genes (nka-α, nka-β, nkcc, nhe) were upregulated in all treatment groups, exhibiting a certain degree of dose-dependence. However, the expression levels of aqp and tip4 genes were significantly downregulated in the TG3 group. While oxidative stress and osmoregulatory function was significantly increased in all stress groups, the most pronounced damage to the gill tissue metabolism was observed in the medium and high concentrations of MC-LR. Metabolomic analysis further demonstrated that MC-LR exposure at 10 μg·L⁻¹ and 20 μg·L⁻¹ elicited broader metabolic perturbations, which may be related to tissue stress injury and the elevated energy requirements for osmoregulation, given that the contents of ATP, glucose, MDH, SDH, and LDH, along with the ammonia excretion rate, were all increased across the experimental groups.

abstract: Multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) cause serious infections that are difficult to treat, leading to increased morbidity and mortality, longer hospital stays, and increased healthcare costs. Many risk factors for MDRO infections are present in the Veteran population (such as older age, underlying medical conditions like diabetes, and stays in long-term healthcare settings). Some people can carry these organisms in their gut. Even without current symptoms, carrying these MDROs also increases risk of future infection. Effective, easy to use, and inexpensive interventions to reduce gut carriage of MDROs are needed to reduce risk of infection. Dietary fiber prebiotics have shown promise in improving the healthy gut microbiome, and the investigators have found that individuals with high fiber in their diets have reduced carriage of MDROs in the gut. The investigators propose a randomized controlled trial to test the effectiveness of a dietary fiber prebiotic intervention (resistant potato starch) in reducing gut MDRO carriage in Veterans with a history of MDRO carriage and/or infection. The investigators will also evaluate the effect on the gut microbiome as well as Veterans' experience with the fiber intervention.

abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize a highly occult subtype of sphenoid invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (IFRS) presenting as acute orbital apex syndrome (OAS) without classic invasive imaging signs, and to evaluate the efficacy of early surgical intervention. METHODS: This retrospective case series evaluated six patients (March 2021-November 2025) who developed classic OAS secondary to sphenoid IFRS despite strictly subtle imaging manifestations. All underwent navigation-guided endoscopic sinus clearance and optic nerve decompression. Pre- and postoperative neuro-ophthalmic parameters (best-corrected visual acuity [BCVA], visual field index [VFI], mean deviation [MD], and ocular motility) were analyzed. Bias-corrected effect sizes (Hedges' g) were calculated to quantify the magnitude of functional recovery. RESULTS: Pathological evaluation confirmed Aspergillus fumigatus (n=4), Penicillium citrinum (n=1), and Rhizopus oryzae (n=1). Four patients (66.7%) had comorbid type 2 diabetes. Following surgery, median BCVA improved from 1.91 to 0.30 LogMAR (Hedges' g = 0.80). In the four patients completing visual field testing, median VFI improved from 11% to 91.5% (g = 1.37), and median MD improved from -28.02 to -3.33 dB (g = 1.23). Ocular motility fully recovered in two of three affected patients. Notably, the two patients lacking visual recovery presented with severe preoperative hyperglycemia (>14 mmol/L). No severe surgery-related complications occurred. CONCLUSIONS: For occult IFRS presenting with this striking 'clinical-radiological dissociation', early navigation-guided endoscopic exploration is a crucial sight-saving strategy. Strict glycemic control is paramount to preserving this therapeutic window. Further prospective validation is warranted.

abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop consensus-based, pragmatic recommendations for the diagnosis and management of fungal pneumonia in non-neutropenic critically ill adults in India and Asia, where the dual burden of mucormycosis and resource-limited healthcare settings creates distinct challenges. METHODS: Using a modified Delphi process, 20 multidisciplinary experts participated in the first round, and 19 completed the second and third rounds of anonymous voting on risk factors, diagnostic strategies, and management of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA), pulmonary mucormycosis (PM), and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP). Consensus was defined as ≥ 70% agreement or disagreement; statements with 60-69% agreement were categorized as "suggest," while the remaining were classified as "no consensus." RESULTS: Key risk factors included severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, influenza, COVID-19, diabetes mellitus, and chronic liver or kidney disease. A multimodal diagnostic strategy combining contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), early bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), microscopy, culture, and galactomannan (BAL threshold ≥ 1.0) was recommended, with molecular methods used where available. Liposomal amphotericin B was the preferred empiric agent in regions with high mucormycosis prevalence; voriconazole, posaconazole, or isavuconazole are first-line for proven IPA. Therapeutic drug monitoring is essential for azole antifungals, with a minimum treatment duration of 6-12 weeks. For PCP, empiric trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is recommended in immunosuppressed patients with diffuse ground-glass opacities on CT after exclusion of competing diagnoses. Adjunctive corticosteroids are recommended for PCP with severe hypoxemia (PaO₂ <70 mmHg) despite limited evidence in non-HIV patients. CONCLUSION: We provide practical, resource-adapted guidance for managing fungal pneumonia in non-neutropenic ICU patients, while highlighting research priorities. The proposed diagnostic criteria for IPA and PM are provisional consensus-based frameworks intended to support clinical decision-making and require prospective multicentre validation. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Direct analysis in real time (DART) is a soft ionization technique that uses a heated gas such as helium, argon, or nitrogen to generate a cascade of ionized atmospheric molecules that subsequently ionize analytes in biological samples. OBJECTIVES: In this proof-of-concept study evaluating selected antifungals in human serum, 5-fluorocytosine (5FC), itraconazole (ITR), hydroxyitraconazole (OH-ITR), isavuconazole (ISV), ketoconazole (KETO), fluconazole (FLU), and posaconazole (POSA) were assessed as DART candidates using a Bruker EVOQ® DART-TQ+. METHODS: Human serum samples were extracted using protein precipitation or liquid-liquid extraction. Quantification was performed by DART tandem mass spectrometry (DART-MS/MS) with internal standards. Precision and linearity across individual analytical measurement ranges (AMRs) were evaluated with rapid sample acquisition (0.24 min linear scans), and the results were compared with those obtained using validated LC-MS/MS methods. A moderate linear association with bias for POSA was likely attributable to matrix effects. More selective sample preparation may improve DART accuracy. Overall, DART-MS/MS shows promise as a rapid, high-throughput alternative to conventional LC-MS/MS. Researchers tested a fast mass spectrometry technique (direct analysis in real time tandem mass spectrometry, DART-MS/MS) to measure antifungal drugs in human blood serum. Using simple extraction steps, they analyzed seven common medications and compared the results with those obtained using a standard liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) lab method. For most drugs, accuracy, precision, and linearity were good and matched those of the reference method. Posaconazole showed some bias, likely from sample matrix effects. abstract: BACKGROUND: Contact precautions are used commonly to prevent nosocomial transmission of methicillin-resistant RESEARCH QUESTION: Compared with standard contact precautions, are targeted contact precautions able to reduce the number of days patients spend in contact precautions and are they as effective at preventing hospital-acquired infection with MRSA and VRE? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A pragmatic, single-center, single-cluster, crossover pilot and feasibility trial in which all adults admitted to a single medical ICU alternated every 2 months between targeted and standard contact precautions for MRSA and VRE for a total of 8 months. In targeted periods, patients received contact precautions only for highly transmissible MRSA or VRE infections, including open wounds, uncontrolled diarrhea, or pneumonia. In standard periods, patients received contact precautions for any MRSA or VRE infection or colonization. The primary pilot outcome was hospital-acquired infection with MRSA or VRE.
